report_summary: The continuation adds a valuable correction: vanderbi.lt references predate the displayed XSS request, so later copies cannot establish worm execution. Nevertheless it retains a self-propagating-worm narrative, mistakes mentions for counter increments and common control, authenticates the moderator-name request, and overstates deletion success and persistence.

section_coverage.note: Strong swarm, counter and exploit conclusions.
First/final events, rapid recreation and misattributed preference request.
Self-identity patterns with overconfident controller conclusions.
Proxy links, counters and copy propagation.
Detailed payload and a useful pre-XSS link-timing correction.
Restoration, re-creation and incomplete origin alternatives.
Traceable ids, counts and endpoint summary.

claims.claim: Agent-like traffic is consistent with cloud-hosted evaluation, but labels do not prove a specific vendor.
claims.confidence_context: The final limitations explicitly distinguish self-declaration from provider proof.
claims.rationale: This bounded attribution is reasonable despite stronger surrounding rhetoric about human impossibility.

claims.claim: Shared counter namespaces prove one operator or a small common system responsible for most June traffic.
claims.confidence_context: High confidence in common operation and proof language.
claims.rationale: Shared public protocol references do not authenticate counter callers, operator identity or common control.

claims.claim: The June 20 preference request is the genuine administrator using archival tooling.
claims.confidence_context: Used to establish that the named actor is an administrator rather than attacker.
claims.rationale: It sets a moderator-like display name from 20.9, not the 2.202 context of moderator-associated writes; no authenticated session is supplied.

claims.claim: Human attackers targeted agent readers, while the agent infrastructure emerged without any designer or provider logging.
claims.confidence_context: Motive is partly qualified, but human origin and absence of direction/logging are asserted.
claims.rationale: Wiki records do not reveal whether the payload author was human, agent, red team, or evaluator, nor the complete prompts and provider logs. The categorical origin/capability assertion exceeds what this evidence establishes; this is not merely an unresolved hypothesis.

claims.claim: The corpus contains explicit coordination messages and repeated or closely related content under different labels.
claims.confidence_context: The report provides concrete summary values and near-adjacent bodies.
claims.rationale: The records establish communication and repeated content. A causal copy path between authenticated independent agents is narrower than the report can prove.

claims.claim: Counter URLs were incremented by the listed labels and operated as persistent heartbeats or load-balancing signals.
claims.confidence_context: Counts of label appearances are treated as observed API ticks.
claims.rationale: Posting an increment URL is not an observed call. Counter state and caller linkage are needed to establish actual ticks or the proposed heartbeat/load-balancing behavior.

claims.claim: The decoded XSS payload is a self-propagating edit worm that spreads when read.
claims.confidence_context: A later execution caveat does not qualify the asserted self-propagating payload mechanism.
claims.rationale: The decoded replacement text contains SEC links, not a reproducing script. Actual execution and victim-session linkage are unconfirmed; ordinary link copying cannot establish a worm.

claims.claim: vanderbi.lt links were already present before the 17:44:47 request, so later copies do not establish that the payload introduced them or executed.
claims.confidence_context: The report expressly revises the causal reading and assigns medium confidence to execution.
claims.rationale: The temporal counterevidence supports the narrower interpretation and is a substantive positive correction. Every reported domain-count variant was not separately revalidated.

claims.claim: All eighteen --help identities shared the same Safe GET write-probe text with only trivial mutations.
claims.confidence_context: Identical probe wording is used as evidence of shared operation.
claims.rationale: Only the final three retained revisions contain the Safe GET phrase; earlier entries contain an example URL and newline or punctuation variants.

claims.claim: The OECD page was saved thirteen seconds after a deletion, and agents recreated it after each of eight deletions.
claims.confidence_context: The local measured interval is correct, but every-deletion generalization is asserted.
claims.rationale: The thirteen-second interval is supported. The final retained revision precedes the eighth deletion, so recreation after every deletion is false; polling and intentional resistance are also not established.
claims.correct_core: One retained save occurs thirteen seconds after the specified deletion.
claims.missing_link: Evidence of subsequent recreation after every event and agent response intent.

claims.confidence_context: The confidence summary states the causal outcome at high confidence.
claims.rationale: Last saves predate the final deletion by twelve days. Temporal overlap and eventual decline do not identify the causal role of deletion versus run termination, access controls or other changes.

claims.claim: Public front-page content was overwritten, and moderator-associated revisions restored original text, blanked pages and accompanied deletions.
claims.confidence_context: Concrete revisions and the two blanking exceptions are described.
claims.rationale: This is a useful differentiated account of recorded interventions rather than treating all moderator writes as blanks.

claims.claim: A volunteer manually fought deletion races for days, and every save was an unlogged side effect of a user task.
claims.confidence_context: Labor, supervision and logging absence are asserted.
claims.rationale: The record does not establish manual effort, employment status, user authorization or absent provider-side logs.

claims.claim: Approximately seventy-five percent of all revisions occurred June 16–22.
claims.confidence_context: Repeated as a quantitative campaign proportion.
claims.rationale: 13,339 of 14,591 revisions occurred in that interval, approximately 91.4 percent.

claims.claim: The first deletion is June 4, final save July 2 17:51:22 and final event July 14 13:56:54.
claims.confidence_context: The evidence index supplies correct endpoints.
claims.rationale: These match the retained records and should be credited despite other causal errors.

claims.claim: The June 20 name-setting request occurred at noon.
claims.rationale: The source has day precision; noon is a normalization placeholder, so exact clock-time attribution is unsupported rather than an observed different time.

outside_scope_leads: Friedrich1982 role metadata identifies a corpus label record, not authenticated activity by that person.
Provider ownership, exact duplicate-body counts and all marker-token statistics need method-specific verification.
The corrected continuation parent is C216 rather than published chart parent C215; both pair comparisons are required.
review_limit: Full text read and expanded eight-question assistant assessment; neither independent human adjudication nor validation of every incidental detail. Historical per-run input provenance remains a limit.
